model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Recorded identity is this evaluating session's ACTUAL runtime model, per #1058: the session runs as Opus 5 (1M context), exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. The agent definition's frontmatter pin was NOT copied into these fields; the pin selects the evaluator, this record states which one ran. Scores here are comparable only to other evaluations produced by claude-opus-5[1m].

divergences_from_own_definition: APPLICABILITY (#1079): my loaded agent definition gates BOTH Element 8 sub-elements 3 and 4 on the 'software tools produced as dataset output' condition (a referenced code repository, or software production named as a dataset output). The launcher's quoted #1079 removes that gate from sub-element 4, making it applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields, and confines the gating paragraph to sub-element 3. I applied the launcher's quoted rule. The outcome is unchanged here: under my own definition the condition is borderline (external_resources points at a GitHub organisation root, not a repository) and the ambiguity rule would default it to applicable anyway.

THRESHOLD (#1059): my loaded definition says a pointer identifying only the publisher (an organisation root such as github.com/<org>, a project homepage, or prose saying code was 'released via GitHub') 'scores 0'. The launcher's quoted #1059 says such a pointer 'neither earns nor forfeits the point' — i.e. neutral rather than disqualifying. I applied the launcher's neutral reading. The outcome is unchanged here: the record scores 0 under case (a) because no slot names the processing software at all, not because of how github.com/AI-READI is treated.

SLOT LIST (#1059): my definition qualifies 'the tool fields of preprocessing_strategies' and 'external_resources pointing at a code repository'. The quoted rule is broader: 'any field of preprocessing_strategies including its prose, or external_resources'. I applied the broader quoted list and read the full preprocessing_strategies prose; it names data standards and file formats, not software.

ELEMENT 4 (#1060): my loaded definition already carries the per-sub-element applicability rule as quoted (sub-elements 1-2 open on the human-subjects condition OR an applying governance constraint; sub-elements 3-5 open only on the human-subjects condition). No divergence. Moot for this record: the human-subjects condition is met on Element 1 and Element 8 evidence, so all five sub-elements are applicable.
rule_provenance.independence_attestation: No file under data/evaluation_llm/ was opened at any point during this evaluation. The only files read were the target D4D YAML and directory listings; hashes were computed over the target and over data/rubric/rubric10.txt.

issues_detected.description: Preprocessing and cleaning are described at length but no processing software is ever named. preprocessing_strategies names data standards and target formats (OMOP Common Data Model, DICOM, Open mHealth) and states that 'Processing for this release combined automated and custom steps', which explicitly declines to identify the tooling. There is no software_and_tools slot, no machine_annotation_tools slot, and external_resources points at the AI-READI GitHub organisation root rather than at any repository. A reader cannot determine what software produced the distributed release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add software_and_tools naming the conversion and standardisation pipelines (the .fda/.sdt to DICOM converters, the .FIT to Open mHealth converter, the OMOP mapping tooling) with versions and the specific repositories under github.com/AI-READI that hold them.

issues_detected.description: Institutional attribution is internally contradictory and carried unresolved. data_governance.accountable_organization and creators.affiliations lead with Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268), while human_subject_research.ethics_review_board and ethical_reviews name the University of Washington IRB, and funders records award OT2OD032644 whose RePORTER awardee is the University of Washington. The record discloses the conflict in source_caveats and reports rather than reconciles it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Resolve the Licensor/awardee/IRB attribution with the consortium, or state explicitly which organisation holds which role rather than letting one name lead the governance fields while another leads the ethics fields.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified carries three mutually inconsistent source statements in one block: identifiable_elements_present is false, method is asserted as 'HIPAA Safe Harbor', yet deidentification_details records FAIRhub's de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary, while the RO-Crate records the release as deidentified. The chosen method value is not the value the tier-1 platform metadata states.
issues_detected.recommendation: State which statement governs the released files and why, rather than asserting a method in the structured slot that the platform metadata contradicts in the prose slot beneath it.

issues_detected.description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted' while the record's own other_compliance reports the RO-Crate value as 'HL7:2N (normal)', and confidential_elements_present and sensitive_elements_present are both false. The record gives its reasoning (verified-ID login and license assent gate access), so this is a defensible escalation rather than an error, but the structured value diverges from the cited source value.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the escalation but record the source value in the structured slot's own note so a consumer reading only the enum is not misled about provenance.

issues_detected.description: sampling_strategies sets is_sample to false while the same block describes an explicit non-probability sampling design with EHR ICD-10 screening, recruitment waves, and deliberate under- and oversampling by race/ethnicity, sex and T2DM severity. The notes reconcile this (the healthsheet answers that the release contains all enrolled participants), but the boolean and the narrative read against each other.
issues_detected.recommendation: Scope the boolean explicitly to 'all enrolled participants are included' so it is not read as a claim that no sampling design exists.

issues_detected.description: file_collections total_bytes sum to 3,815,969,360,064 against a stated total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678, a shortfall of 419,614 bytes. The root_metadata collection carries a file_count of 9 but no total_bytes, which accounts for the gap in kind. The record discloses the discrepancy in source_caveats.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate total_bytes on the root_metadata collection so the per-collection sizes reconcile to the stated dataset total.

issues_detected.description: The variables block gives 20 fully specified variables with data types, units, descriptions and measurement techniques, but carries no ontology or term identifiers, and the record itself states that the authoritative per-domain variable documentation at docs.aireadi.org was not in the input bundle. For a release of 356,343 files spanning OMOP clinical tables, this is a representative sample rather than a data dictionary.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach LOINC/SNOMED/OMOP concept identifiers to the listed variables and link the per-domain variable documentation as the authoritative dictionary.

issues_detected.description: No download_url slot is populated. Retrieval is nonetheless documented through page, data_governance.access_review_process (FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' plus the conditions-of-access URL) and third_party_sharing, so a user can reach the data; the dedicated slot is simply empty.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub download endpoint so machine consumers do not have to infer retrieval from the governance prose.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 is well formed and its prefix is FAIRhub's own, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 — identifier, publisher and landing page agree.

All three grant numbers match NIH patterns: OT2OD032644 (OT2 activity code, OD institute), P30DK035816 (P30 centre grant, NIDDK) and UL1TR003096 (UL1 CTSA, NCATS). The record explains that the tier-1 platform metadata records only OT2OD032644 and that the other two come from the protocol publication.

Participant arithmetic is internally exact: instances.counts 2280 equals the diabetes-status subpopulation sum (776 + 560 + 686 + 258), the sex sum (951 + 1329), and the recommended split (1576 + 352 + 352).

File counts reconcile exactly: the nine data-type collections sum to 356,334 and the root_metadata collection's 9 files bring the total to the stated 356,343. The record's own caveat treats this as an unexplained nine-file shortfall; it is in fact reconciled by its own root_metadata entry.
Temporal ordering is coherent: collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, issued 2025-11-17, and distribution_dates ascending across v1.0.0 (2024-05-03), v2.0.0 (2024-11-08) and v3.0.0 (2025-11-17).

Version lineage cross-references resolve: related_datasets is_new_version_of targets doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and fairhub.1 match the DOIs and participant counts recorded in version_access.versions_available.

Human-subjects logic is fully satisfied: involves_human_subjects true is matched by IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with an approval date and named reliance agreements, by written and electronic consent with a stated withdrawal mechanism, and by a documented $200 compensation scheme.

The negative answers are substantive rather than empty: content_warnings, confidential_elements and sensitive_elements are each false with a stated basis, and instances.label is false with a description explaining that the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic so no annotation software or annotator information applies.

Bias documentation uses the schema's bias_type taxonomy (selection_bias, representation_bias, sampling_bias) and pairs two of the four entries with concrete mitigation strategies including the triple-balanced recruitment design and the balanced recommended splits.

Standards conformance is unusually specific and per-modality: CDS v0.1.1 directory layout, WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical, DICOM for all four imaging types, Open mHealth for wearables and CGM, NASA ESDS for environmental sensing, plus an RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT / FAIRscape 0.1 packaging.

Collection mechanisms are documented device by device across 21 entries with make, model, protocol and acquisition settings, which is the strongest element of the record and materially exceeds what the sub-element asks for.

The record's discipline about source disagreement is a genuine quality signal: enrollment start date, license name, institutional attribution, grant count and de-identification status each carry an explicit source_caveats block naming the conflicting tiers and the value chosen.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: Matches the 10.XXXX/... pattern. Prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's own registered prefix and agrees with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3, so format and registrar plausibility both hold. No RRID is claimed.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project; description: ~1,400 characters naming three collection sites, 2280 participants, the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window, 356,343 files, 3.82 TB, and every modality from OMOP-mapped clinical data through FLIO and home environmental sensing.
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character bar and specific throughout. It also states the study design rationale (balanced recruitment for salutogenesis analysis) and what was removed before public release.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam]
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven keywords meeting the five-keyword bar, covering condition, method and modality. Slightly narrow for a dataset this broad, since environmental sensing and wearable activity are not represented.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections with ten entries, the root_metadata entry carrying a nested resources list of nine named metadata files with formats and descriptions.
sub_elements.quality_note: Active landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical resource structure: collection, then per-file resources with ids minted on the dataset DOI.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2; is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; has_part 'AI-READI mini-subset version of the dataset'
sub_elements.quality_note: Three typed relationships with participant counts and release dates. The mini-subset entry honestly records that no identifier exists in the sources and explains why a containment relation was chosen over a derivation one.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms describing the AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 with storage, BAA, derivative-work and termination clauses; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions.restrictions on title, model distribution and watermarking.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both slots substantive. The access policy states the concrete gate (verified-ID login plus attestation to T2DM-only research) rather than naming a licence in the abstract.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions listing NIH Genomic Data Sharing security standards and watermarking obligations; other_compliance recording non-FDA-regulated status and the RO-Crate HL7:2N value.
sub_elements.quality_note: All three of the sub-element's fields populated with named frameworks. Flagged separately as a low-severity issue that the chosen enum diverges from the cited RO-Crate value, with the record's reasoning given.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; data_governance.access_review_process: 'FAIRhub records the access type as "PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired" and publishes the conditions of access at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; third_party_sharing describing distribution through FAIRhub under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3.
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element accepts platform access instructions and these are precise: the platform, the access endpoint, the access type and the two conditions a requester must satisfy. Scored 1 on that basis with the empty slot recorded as an issue.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json), Markdown (text/markdown), each with a description of which content it carries; file_collections conforms_to per collection.
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats paired with correct MIME types and mapped to specific data types, so a consumer knows which format holds which modality.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets (3 typed entries); external_resources (9 entries) covering docs.aireadi.org, aireadi.org, the FAIRhub access page, the Zenodo community, the GitHub organisation, the archived licence DOI, the Nature Metabolism comment, the BMJ Open protocol and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048.
sub_elements.quality_note: Every entry carries a resolvable URL or DOI and a description of what it contains. The documentation entry also records its own CC-BY 4.0 terms.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET. distribution_formats is populated with four formats, page and the FAIRhub access endpoint resolve to an accessible release, and the licence explicitly grants rights to download, reproduce and create derivative works. Sub-elements 1-4 are therefore applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated (DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown); page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 with a stated access route; licence grants download, reproduction and derivative-work rights for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'It grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes.'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse permissions are stated affirmatively, with the boundaries (storage location, BAA requirement, secondary-sharing limits, automatic termination) spelled out. A custom licence rather than a standard CC instrument, but its terms are recorded in enough detail to be actionable.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats with format and media_type pairs; conforms_to naming WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth and the NASA ASCII File Format Guidelines per modality.
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are standard and mapped per data type. Character encoding is never stated anywhere in the record, which is the one gap; the format documentation is strong enough that the sub-element's purpose is met.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to describing CDS v0.1.1 layout plus per-modality standards; conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Both prose and enumerated forms present, and each file_collection repeats its own conforms_to_standard so conformance is stated at the level a consumer actually reads.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: 20 entries, each with variable_name, data_type and description; units on blood glucose (mg/dL), visual acuity (logMAR), contrast sensitivity (log contrast sensitivity), HbA1c (%), urine albumin and creatinine (mg/dL); measurement_technique on every entry; maximum_value 30.0 and quality_notes where relevant.
sub_elements.quality_note: Well beyond boilerplate: each variable names the instrument that produced it, and the visual acuity entry records that Snellen variables were dropped in 3.0.0. No ontology or OMOP concept identifiers are attached, and the record states the authoritative per-domain dictionary was outside the bundle, so this is a representative sample rather than complete coverage. Recorded as a low-severity issue; the content present is meaningful and actionable, so the point holds.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: two categories with usage_notes and an example of permitted model distribution; prohibited_uses: six entries covering clinical decision-making, re-identification attempts, third-party model-vendor sharing, onward conveyance, publication volume limits and watermark removal, each with a stated reason.
sub_elements.quality_note: The strongest use-guidance block in the record. Every prohibition gives the protective rationale, and the third-party model-vendor clause is unusually specific about what remains allowed (short-term prompting under a BAA).

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Per-sub-element applicability applied as quoted (#1060). Human-subjects condition resolved from Element 1 and Element 8 fields only, never from Element 4's own fields: description states data were 'collected from individuals with and without T2DM' and reports 2280 participants; keywords include 'Diabetes mellitus'; collection_mechanisms describes participant recruitment via personalised REDCap invitations, in-person study visits and 10 days of at-home device wear. Condition MET, so sub-elements 1-2 open on the human-subjects disjunct (the governance disjunct is not needed) and sub-elements 3-5 open on the human-subjects condition. All five applicable.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: E1 description: 'collected from individuals with and without T2DM ... data from 2280 participants'; E1 keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus'; E8 collection_mechanisms: participant recruitment through a REDCap recruitment interface, in-visit questionnaires and take-home devices. Human-subjects condition met on E1/E8 evidence.
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.irb_approval: 'Protocol STUDY00016228; initial IRB approval received on December 20, 2022 ... Reliance agreements were in place with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego.'; ethics_review_board: University of Washington IRB with Human Subjects Division address and hsdrely@uw.edu; ethical_reviews with a second entry naming the AI-READI ethics reviewers.
sub_elements.quality_note: involves_human_subjects is true and the expected IRB detail is present with protocol number, approval date, renewal requirement and reliance structure. A named bioethics review team is documented alongside the regulatory review, and data_governance.committee_contact gives a governance contact. Consistency check passes.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E8 human-subjects evidence as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified: identifiable_elements_present: false; method: HIPAA Safe Harbor; identifiers_removed: 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule; participant sex; race/ethnicity; medications used'; deidentification_details recording the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' statement, the Safe Harbor stripping and the RO-Crate deidentified flag.
sub_elements.quality_note: A named method with an explicit identifier list, plus disclosure that the release was internally reviewed but never externally audited. Safe Harbor is an appropriate method for a health dataset of this type. The three conflicting source statements carried in one block are recorded as a medium-severity content-accuracy issue; the method is nonetheless described in enough detail to be assessed, so the point holds.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 description and keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms, as above. This sub-element opens only on that condition; no governance-structure disjunct was used.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor removal; participants appear only under study IDs); privacy_techniques (variable removal, static watermarking, licence prohibitions on identification attempts, verified-ID gating, encrypted servers and locked storage during collection); reidentification_risk ('a theoretical risk of future re-identification'); data_linkage (files organised by participant ID so modalities link within the release).
sub_elements.quality_note: All four privacy fields populated, and the re-identification risk is stated explicitly rather than implied. future_use_impacts extends it with the specific mechanism of concern, that AI algorithms can infer patient characteristics, and names the three mitigations. Consistency check between data_protection_impacts-style content and reidentification_risk passes.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1/E8 evidence, as above.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent: consent_obtained: true; consent_type 'Written informed consent, obtained either electronically (e-consent with electronic signature in REDCap) or in person'; consent_documentation; consent_scope recording the FAIRhub consent type and the T2DM-only restriction on the public version; withdrawal_mechanism. Also collection_consents and consent_revocations.
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent type, documentation, scope and withdrawal are all specified, and the withdrawal clause is honest about its limit: data already shared or used stay in the dataset. The reliance sites are recorded as using the same form with minor institution-specific language. IRB-implies-consent consistency check passes.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1/E8 evidence, as above.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations: at_risk_groups_included: false with special_protections ('Minors are excluded by the minimum age of 40 years; pregnancy and gestational diabetes are exclusion criteria; the IRB protocol records that the research is not likely to have subjects who become prisoners'); participant_compensation: compensation_provided true, $200, stipend type covering parking, transit and rideshare, with payment timing and the $25 transport cap in notes.
sub_elements.quality_note: The negative answer on at-risk groups is substantiated by the specific eligibility rules that produce it rather than left as a bare false. Compensation is documented to an unusual level, including when it is paid and what is not reimbursed.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: four entries (self-reported race/ethnicity, biological sex, diabetes status group, age), each with identification and distribution; aggregate counts 380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White; 951 male, 1329 female; mean age 60.8 ± 11.3; eligibility 40 years and older.
sub_elements.quality_note: Demographics, inclusion criteria and group definitions all present. The subpopulation_elements_present flags correctly distinguish the two variables removed from the public release from the two that remain, and aggregate counts are still supplied for the removed ones.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances.counts: 2280; total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; splits recording training 1576, validation 352, test 352; per-collection file_count values across ten file_collections.
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are given at participant, file and byte level and at the split level. The participant arithmetic is internally exact across three independent breakdowns, and the split flags are carried as a dedicated splits block with the 70/15/15 rationale.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: variables: 20 entries with data_type, unit, description and measurement_technique; is_tabular: false.
sub_elements.quality_note: The tabular flag is correct and meaningful for a release that is predominantly DICOM imaging and waveform data. Variable coverage is a documented sample rather than the full dictionary, noted as a low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances.instance_type: 'Individual study participant'; data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43; notes listing the six modality families that constitute an instance; file_collections describing each data type in clinical terms.
sub_elements.quality_note: A coded topic identifier plus a prose account of what one instance contains. The condition under study, type 2 diabetes across four severity strata, is unambiguous from description, subpopulations and instances together.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries covering survey skips, wearable charging gaps on the Garmin Vivosmart 5, imaging noise and transfer failures, undilated handheld fundus variability, FLIO comfort and movement tolerance, and manual-device skipping; sampling_strategies; missing_data_documentation with missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy.
sub_elements.quality_note: Device-specific rather than generic, which is what makes it usable. The handling strategy names who decided (site principal investigator) and states that no imputation of missing modality data was performed and no instances were excluded at preprocessing.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET (distribution_formats populated, accessible FAIRhub page and access endpoint, licence permits reuse). All five sub-elements applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated; page and access endpoint resolve; licence grants reuse rights.
sub_elements.evidence: version: '3.0.0'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: Semantic version present and consistent with the DOI, the citation string and the related_datasets lineage.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition.
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.versions_available listing all three versions with DOIs, release dates and participant counts; version_details: 'All versions are listed on the FAIRhub dataset page and each has its own documentation set at docs.aireadi.org; version 2.0.0 is marked as no longer accessible.'
sub_elements.quality_note: States how to reach each version and, importantly, which one is no longer retrievable. Each historical version carries its own resolvable DOI.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition.
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.version_details: 'version 3.0.0 adds the second and third years of data collection, adds imaging devices relative to the pilot, moves from custom/ad hoc to automated plus custom processing, and drops the Snellen visual acuity variables'; file_collections resources includes CHANGELOG.md described as recording the changes between versions; variables quality_notes repeating the Snellen removal.
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete change descriptions at the level of specific variables and processing methods, and the changelog file is registered as a resource. No errata slot exists and no errata are claimed; the change-description half of the sub-element is met substantively.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition.
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Approximately annually'; update_details: 'released as static versions and is not updated in place; rather, new versions are released with additional instances ... enrollment is ongoing, so future versions are expected to include larger numbers of participants.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the cadence and the update model are stated, and the static-versioning policy tells a consumer that a pinned DOI will not shift under them.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same shared-and-reusable condition.
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: two entries covering EHR screening (used for recruitment only, not released) and device-native exports (.xml, .csv, .fda, .sdt, .FIT, DICOM) with access_details explaining why raw data are retained but not shared; related_datasets version lineage; distribution_dates for all three releases.
sub_elements.quality_note: The derivation chain from device-native export through standardisation to the released format is traceable, and the raw-data retention and non-release decision is justified (unmapped terminologies, possible free-text PHI). No was_derived_from or release_notes slots, but raw_data_sources is one of the sub-element's own listed fields and carries the weight.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four responses covering AI/ML insight into T2DM and salutogenic pathways, public sharing of a balanced multimodal dataset, a foundational dataset agnostic to existing classification criteria, and a blueprint for future data generation projects; addressing_gaps: three responses on the absence of large inclusive multimodal datasets and the demographic imbalance found in a 2000-2020 meta-epidemiological review.
sub_elements.quality_note: Scientific rationale and the specific research gap are both articulated, with the gap statement citing evidence rather than asserting novelty.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: pseudo-time manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories across severity strata, and development of AI/ML models of salutogenesis and multimodal models; other_tasks recording that the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and unlabelled so downstream users define their own tasks.
sub_elements.quality_note: Named analytical methods rather than generic 'machine learning', and the other_tasks entry is honest that no formal guidelines exist for user-defined tasks.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health with the award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project' made through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program; Research to Prevent Blindness; Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services).
sub_elements.quality_note: Three funders with the funding mechanism named for the primary award, plus in-kind support identified separately. The source_caveats block explains why publication-only grants are retained alongside the tier-1 funding reference.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: grant_number: OT2OD032644 (notes record RePORTER project number 1OT2OD032644-01, $5,026,499 for FY2022, project period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31); grant_number: P30DK035816; grant_number: UL1TR003096
sub_elements.quality_note: All three match NIH award patterns: OT2/OD, P30/DK (NIDDK centre grant) and UL1/TR (NCATS CTSA). The primary award carries amount and period detail. Semantic check passes for all three; format validation returns valid.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: AI-READI Consortium with principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) and nine affiliations each carrying a ROR identifier; data_collectors notes acknowledging that team effort was supported by NIH award OT2OD032644.
sub_elements.quality_note: Creator, PI with a resolvable ORCID, and institutional affiliations with ROR identifiers throughout. The PI's own source_caveats records the Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington affiliation conflict rather than silently picking one.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
elements.applicability_note: Sub-elements 1-2: data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms both richly populated) AND datasets shared (distribution_formats, accessible FAIRhub endpoint, reuse licence) — both halves MET, applicable. Sub-element 3: gated on the software-tools-as-output condition; external_resources references https://github.com/AI-READI, an organisation root rather than a named repository, which makes the condition borderline, so the ambiguity rule defaults it to applicable and scored. Sub-element 4: per the quoted #1079, NOT gated on that condition — applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established here from preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies; applicable and scored. Sub-element 5: shared-and-reusable condition met, applicable.

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms are populated with 2 and 21 entries. Datasets shared: distribution_formats populated, FAIRhub access endpoint published, licence permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: 21 entries, e.g. '12-lead electrocardiography with the Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph, performed with the participant reclining or supine and the chair position recorded'; 'Visual acuity measured with the M&S Technologies Electronic Visual Acuity (EVA) tester at 4 meters under photopic conditions and under mesopic conditions using a 2.0 neutral density filter'; 'Dexcom G6 ... worn continuously for 10 days after the visit, capturing readings every five minutes'.
sub_elements.quality_note: The strongest block in the record. Device make and model, acquisition protocol, sampling frequency, wear duration and even participant positioning are recorded per modality, which is enough for a reader to judge comparability with their own data.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same conditions as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: directly observed measurements (was_directly_observed: true) and participant-reported REDCap questionnaires (was_reported_by_subjects: true, was_validated_verified: true, with medication cross-referencing against physically brought or photographed medications); raw_data_sources describing device-native export formats before standardisation.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both acquisition modes flagged with the schema's booleans and substantiated in prose. The verification method for self-reported medication data is concrete.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Condition is 'external_resources (from E10) references a code repository, OR description/purposes (from E1/E7) explicitly identifies software production as a dataset output'. external_resources entry 'GitHub organization of the AI-READI project — https://github.com/AI-READI' is an organisation root, not a named repository, and purposes name a 'blueprint' rather than software as an output. The condition is therefore borderline rather than plainly failing, and the ambiguity rule defaults to applicable and scored. Determination made on E10/E1/E7 fields, not on E8's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: mapping to OMOP CDM and DICOM, conversion of Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt to DICOM and Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, and the note that processing 'combined automated and custom steps, in contrast with the custom/ad hoc processing of version 1.0.0'; second entry recording that no instances were excluded at preprocessing; cleaning_strategies describing range flagging in REDCap, credibility and skip-pattern checks, and PI-approved editing or removal; instances.label: false with label_description explaining that no labelling was performed and no annotation software or annotator information applies.
sub_elements.quality_note: Preprocessing and cleaning are documented as a traceable pipeline with named target standards, decision authority and exclusion policy. The labelling answer is a substantive negative rather than an empty slot. No annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols, which is coherent with an unlabelled dataset that performs no imputation of missing modality data.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Per the quoted #1079: applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, NOT gated on whether a repository is pointed at. Processing is established from Element 8's own collection and preprocessing fields as that rule directs: preprocessing_strategies records mapping to OMOP CDM and DICOM and conversion of .fda, .sdt and .FIT exports, and cleaning_strategies records a QC and editing pass. The dataset was processed, so the sub-element is applicable and scored rather than excluded.
sub_elements.slot_searched: software_and_tools (absent), machine_annotation_tools (absent), preprocessing_strategies (all fields including prose, read in full), external_resources (all 9 entries)
sub_elements.evidence: No software_and_tools slot exists in the record and no machine_annotation_tools slot exists. preprocessing_strategies names data standards and target formats only: 'all data were mapped to standardized terminologies where possible, including the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model for clinical data and DICOM for medical imaging; proprietary device exports were transformed into standard model formats before upload to FAIRhub, with Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt files converted to DICOM and Garmin .FIT files converted to the Open mHealth standard. Processing for this release combined automated and custom steps' — OMOP CDM, DICOM and Open mHealth are data models and formats, not software, and the closing sentence explicitly declines to identify the tooling. external_resources contains 'GitHub organization of the AI-READI project — https://github.com/AI-READI'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored 0 under case (a): no slot documenting processing or tooling names the software that produced or processed the distributed data. Which slot carried the evidence: none. The github.com/AI-READI pointer is an organisation root that identifies the publisher rather than the software, so per the quoted rule it neither earns nor forfeits the point — the 0 rests on case (a) independently of it, and would stand even if that pointer were disregarded entirely. Case (b) applies as a secondary observation to the software that IS named elsewhere: REDCap appears in collection_mechanisms and in cleaning_strategies as the data-capture and range-flagging platform, and the MoCA Duo application appears in collection_mechanisms as an instrument — both are capture rather than processing software, and cleaning_strategies is not a slot the threshold lists. The OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is mentioned inside a file_collections description as a tool a consumer may run against dqd_omop.json, which is downstream analysis rather than what produced the release. A reader therefore cannot tell what software converted the vendor exports to DICOM and Open mHealth or performed the OMOP mapping.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, FAIRhub access endpoint published, licence permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: nine entries including the BMJ Open protocol (doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449), the Nature Metabolism comment (https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), docs.aireadi.org, the archived licence DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048; conforms_to and conforms_to_standard naming seven standards.
sub_elements.quality_note: Published papers, standards documents and platform documentation are all referenced with resolvable identifiers, and the trial registration links the dataset to its study record.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries (representativeness, coverage, scope, temporal, methodological), the first carrying scope_impact: 'Models derived from the dataset may not generalize to populations, settings or cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds that the three recruiting health systems do not reach.'
sub_elements.quality_note: Each limitation is typed and states its consequence for downstream use. The temporal entry is specific about why longitudinal analysis is impossible here (one visit, only about 10% returning in year 4).

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: four entries typed selection_bias, representation_bias, sampling_bias and selection_bias, covering volunteer bias, pilot-phase imbalance and the absence of Pacific Islander and Native American participants, urban hospital-based recruitment, and the English-language eligibility requirement; two carry mitigation_strategy. future_use_impacts records the anticipated re-identification concern.
sub_elements.quality_note: Uses the schema's bias_type enumeration rather than free prose, and the English-language entry is a candid disclosure that the eligibility rule worked against the study's own diversity goal. Mitigations are concrete (triple-balanced recruitment, three geographically distinct sites, balanced recommended splits).

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries including 'Undilated handheld fundus photography with the Optomed Aurora is challenging because the pupil is not dilated and the camera is handheld, so image quality varies from patient to patient and within the same patient' and the FLIO entry on acquisition length, light discomfort and one-centimetre movement tolerance.
sub_elements.quality_note: Device-level and mechanism-level rather than generic. These are the anomalies an analyst would need to know before modelling the imaging data.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present: false with 'The public dataset ... carries no protected health information, and information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of participants and to medications used has been removed'; content_warnings: content_warnings_present: false citing the healthsheet answer; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present: false.
sub_elements.quality_note: Three negative determinations, each substantiated by what was removed or by the source that states it, and each consistent with the deidentification block. Meaningful negatives rather than unpopulated slots.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries. First, University of Washington IRB, protocol STUDY00016228, approved December 20 2022, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD, approval letter published with the 3.0.0 documentation, IRB Reliance Team contact given, plus a source_caveats recording the RO-Crate's conflicting 'Washington University IRB' label. Second, AI-READI ethics team with four named reviewers and the statement that ELSI considerations run at every stage with bioethicist guidance.
sub_elements.quality_note: Review details are thorough and the record documents a disagreement between sources about the reviewing organisation rather than papering over it. No conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere in the record, which is the one part of the sub-element left unaddressed; the ethical review documentation itself is strong enough to carry the point.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET, so sub-elements 1 and 3-5 are applicable. Sub-element 2 additionally requires a publication identified elsewhere: external_resources carries the Nature Metabolism comment (doi 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x) and the BMJ Open protocol (doi 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449), so that condition is MET too. All five applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated; FAIRhub landing page and access endpoint resolve; licence permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; third_party_sharing: 'distributed for public use through the FAIRhub platform (https://fairhub.io/) under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3'; maintainers noting hosting on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure.
sub_elements.quality_note: FAIRhub is a recognised biomedical data repository and the DOI prefix, publisher and landing page all agree. The hosting arrangement is named as well as the platform.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified in external_resources: the Nature Metabolism comment (https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x) and the BMJ Open protocol (doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449). Datasets-shared condition also met. Both halves satisfied.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete formatted citation with creator, year, title, version, repository and resolvable DOI, in a form a reference manager can consume directly. Version-specific rather than generic.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE]; conforms_to describing the RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT packaging with the FAIRscape profile 0.1 and one subcrate per data type.
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven community standards, each tied to the data type it governs, plus a packaging standard. Substantially exceeds the sub-element's bar of naming one or two.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org (per-domain documentation, healthsheet, controlled variables, AI-readiness, training prerequisites, shared CC-BY 4.0), aireadi.org (team listing and contact), the FAIRhub access page, the Zenodo community, the GitHub organisation, and three literature and registry references; page as the landing page.
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, project outreach and community presence are all linked, and the documentation entry records its own licence so a reuser knows the docs are freely reusable.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of → doi:10.60775/fairhub.2; is_new_version_of → doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; has_part → 'AI-READI mini-subset version of the dataset'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationship types come from a controlled vocabulary and two of three targets are resolvable DOIs. The unresolvable third is explained: the sources give no identifier for the mini-subset, and the containment relation was chosen because only a FAIRhub parent/child link is stated, not a derivation direction.

strengths: Collection is documented device by device across 21 mechanism entries with make, model, protocol, sampling frequency and acquisition conditions, which makes the imaging and wearable data comparable against other cohorts rather than merely described.

Ethics documentation is complete on every axis the rubric checks: IRB protocol number with approval date and reliance structure, a named bioethics review team, Safe Harbor deidentification with an explicit identifier list, an assessed re-identification risk, written and electronic consent with a candid withdrawal limit, and a fully specified $200 compensation scheme.

The record discloses source disagreement instead of resolving it silently. Enrollment start date, licence name, institutional attribution, grant count and deidentification status each carry a source_caveats block naming the conflicting tiers and the value chosen, which lets a reader audit the judgement rather than inherit it.

Internal arithmetic is exact where it can be checked: 2280 participants reconcile across the diabetes-status strata, the sex breakdown and the recommended train/validation/test split, and the ten file_collections sum precisely to the stated 356,343 files.

Standards conformance is stated per modality (WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth, NASA ESDS) under a CDS v0.1.1 layout and an RO-Crate packaging, so an integrator knows which standard governs which directory.
weaknesses: No processing software is named anywhere. preprocessing_strategies gives target standards and formats and then says processing 'combined automated and custom steps', which is precisely the sentence that should have named the tools; the only code pointer is an organisation root.

Institutional attribution is contradictory across governance and ethics fields, with Washington University in St. Louis leading the accountable organisation and licensor role while the University of Washington holds the IRB and the NIH award. The record reports the conflict rather than resolving it.

The deidentification block asserts HIPAA Safe Harbor as the method while its own detail records the tier-1 platform value as 'NoDeIdentification', leaving a consumer unable to tell which statement governs the released files.

Variable coverage is a 20-entry sample without ontology or OMOP concept identifiers, and the record states the authoritative per-domain dictionary was outside its input bundle, so variable-level integration still requires going to docs.aireadi.org.

The download_url slot is empty and per-collection byte totals fall 419,614 bytes short of the stated dataset size because root_metadata carries no total_bytes, both small machine-readability gaps in an otherwise complete record.
recommendations: Populate software_and_tools with the pipelines that produced the release: the .fda and .sdt to DICOM converters, the .FIT to Open mHealth converter and the OMOP mapping tooling, each with a version and the specific repository under github.com/AI-READI, replacing the organisation-root pointer with named repositories.

Resolve or explicitly partition the Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington attribution across creators.affiliations, data_governance.accountable_organization, human_subject_research.ethics_review_board and license_and_use_terms, stating which organisation holds licensor, awardee and IRB roles.

State which deidentification statement governs the released files and set is_deidentified.method accordingly, keeping the divergent platform and RO-Crate values in the details prose rather than in tension with the structured slot.

Attach LOINC, SNOMED or OMOP concept identifiers to the listed variables and link the per-domain data dictionary as the authoritative source, so variable-level integration does not depend on prose descriptions.
Populate download_url with the FAIRhub download endpoint and add total_bytes to the root_metadata collection so per-collection sizes reconcile to total_size_bytes.
